H1.evidence: create_token now optionally emits via; the actual SDK issuer supplies via=embedded-agent. The unchanged interactive helper refuses any non-null via, while ordinary JWT verification/get_current_user continues accepting it. Real-token probe admitted ordinary authentication, refused interactive authentication with 401 and derived AGENT in _author_kind. The new route test checks AGENT/embedded-agent provenance and 401 on selection/export. All 30 auth unit tests passed independently. Existing unmarked tokens issued before this change remain valid until their existing expiry; no immediate revocation claim.

H2.evidence: open_download resolves verified stored invocation/receipt pairs, scopes to the current default user, acquires the activated reader, snapshots the archive and calls the existing _require_current within session.begin. That path locks subject masters, profile head, run head, disposition head and packaging head before re-resolving evidence/readiness and its grant locks. Exact run/disposition/digest/current-slot comparisons remain in place. published_generation is checked in the same transaction after readiness. Return authorizes a verified snapshot at this guarded instant; it does not promise to revoke bytes already streaming after later authority changes. The superseded-disposition HTTP regression is present. PG execution, lock waiters and invalidation schedules were not independently runnable.

H3.status: FIXED for the original path/byte integrity defect
H3.evidence: The service reuses descriptor-pinned no-follow export-store access and creates a private WorkDirectory copy. _snapshot_archive requires a regular source with the receipted size, hashes all copied bytes with a size-plus-one bound, compares receipt digest/size, checks source generation before/after copying, and rewinds the snapshot. After currentness it compares the published generation again. The response duplicates and streams the snapshot fd rather than reopening the public archive path. The altered-byte refusal and normal scratch cleanup test are present. The separate failure/cancellation ownership defects introduced by the new snapshot/response lifecycle are N1/N2 below; they do not restore the original unverified-path read.

M1.evidence: Rebuilding with the original parent now compares actual draft/provenance and rejects changed actor/content; the added HTTP changed-draft/agent tests are useful. It still does not serialize the outer replay before generating the revision. Two identical genesis requests can both miss _replay, generate distinct candidate UUIDs/timestamps and reach the M8 command guard with different append_command_digest values; one returns a command conflict rather than the recorded success. A deterministic coroutine probe forced both real append functions past the empty receipt read and used the real M8 digest with an in-memory serialized comparison: one tuple and one CommandConflictError resulted even with the same fixed clock. This is a modeled repository boundary, not a PG schedule. A separate real-function replay probe returned revision 2 after candidate_id was omitted (with expected_head_version=1, an invalid genesis shape on a fresh command); changing run_id to another run with identical derived bindings was also accepted. No stable incoming-request identity is recorded/compared; only the derived payload and a subset of request fields are checked. Run/profile reads still precede replay.
M1.scenario: Concurrent retries of a successful append are not reliably idempotent. An update retry can also change its create/update shape without conflict by omitting candidate_id, and output-equivalent runs are collapsed without an explicit documented equivalence rule.
M1.fix: Serialize the packaging append command before replay and before generating UUID/time; compare a stable normalized incoming semantic request or document and enforce an explicit equivalence rule. Bind actor, author class, create/update shape, run identity and expected version consistently, then reuse the recorded revision for exact retries. Preserve the underlying M8 CAS. Add observed simultaneous-identical PG requests and create/update-shape/run-change regressions.

M2.evidence: _run now catches M8Error; ExplorationNotFoundError maps to 404 and other M8 errors to 409. Real-exception probes confirmed CandidateConflictError=409, CommandConflictError=409 and ExplorationNotFoundError=404. The download service call is also inside _run, so its M10 evidence refusals receive the typed API boundary. Stale-CAS HTTP coverage was added. New raw filesystem failures are not automatically domain errors; their resource cleanup is addressed separately in N1.

M3.status: FIXED in test source; PG result builder-supplied
M3.evidence: The new regression starts with a real existing selection/head, stages both replacement selection and CAS via the real repository append, raises before commit, verifies the original head/id/version and (1 selection,1 head), then retries with fresh custody and asserts version 2 and (2 selections,1 head). The injection is after both writes rather than literally between them, which exercises rollback of at least the same uncommitted writes and addresses the prior partial-state/existing-head gap. It is a Python exception/transaction rollback test, not an abrupt-process kill. Existing exact selection replay coverage remains separate. Reviewer could collect but could not execute the PG body.

M.title: Snapshot target creation failure leaks the already-open archive source fd
M.status: CONFIRMED by source and injected ENOSPC probe
M.scenario: _snapshot_archive opens source, then calls work.create(DOWNLOAD_FILE) before entering the try/with that owns source. If target creation fails with ENOSPC, EDQUOT or another OSError, source is never closed. open_download closes work/store but has no reference to this fd. Repeated requests while storage is full can exhaust host descriptors as well as failing the downloads. A probe supplied a real /dev/null descriptor for the source and injected ENOSPC in work.create; os.fstat on the source still succeeded after the function raised. The reviewer manually closed it after measurement.
M.fix: Take ownership of source immediately after os.open (e.g. an ExitStack or enclosing try/finally), and create the target inside that scope. Ensure every acquired fd is reclaimed on failure and map operational filesystem refusal deliberately. Add a target-create ENOSPC/EDQUOT regression asserting no fd/scratch leaks.

M.title: BackgroundTask is not guaranteed cleanup for a failed or cancelled stream
M.status: CONFIRMED source control flow; ASGI 2.4 send-error probe
M.scenario: The Download retains the original snapshot fd, the WorkDirectory fds/flock and export-store fd; the chunks generator owns only an os.dup. The sole Download.close call is a StreamingResponse BackgroundTask. In installed/pinned Starlette 1.6.0, background execution is after streaming rather than in a finally: stream exceptions/cancellation can exit before it runs. A direct invocation of the real route response under ASGI 2.4 with send raising OSError produced ClientDisconnect and never called the supplied Download.close, even when failing before the first chunk. Scratch remains flock-owned and cannot be reclaimed by the normal active-work sweep; fd exhaustion can follow repeated failures. Current Uvicorn advertises ASGI 2.3, so this probe does not claim its ordinary disconnect branch was executed; source shows exceptions/cancellation in that branch also bypass the trailing background call.
M.fix: Own Download around the response ASGI call with unconditional finally cleanup, including failure before iteration starts; make close safe to invoke exactly once/idempotently. Closing only the duplicated generator handle is insufficient. Add send/read failure, early disconnect and response cancellation tests checking all descriptors, flock and scratch removal. Also audit cancellation during to_thread snapshot acquisition so a worker result cannot outlive its cleanup owner; no completed cancellation-during-copy execution is claimed here.
